Question B-006-012-006.

Why the correct answer is right: An end-fed half-wave antenna can be used on multiple bands because the same wire can operate on harmonic half-wave resonances when it is matched properly.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Matching network not needed to feed with coaxial cable": An EFHW has a high end impedance and normally needs a transformer or matching network to feed it from low-impedance coax.
- sourceIndex 2: "High resistance to local noise pickup": End-fed wires can still pick up local noise, especially through common-mode current on the feedline. Noise immunity is not their major advantage.
- sourceIndex 3: "Develops minimal common-mode current": An EFHW often needs a counterpoise and choking because common-mode current can occur on the outside of the coax. Minimal common-mode current is not guaranteed.
